title: Cap. X controversy-sum: if in the eternal decree some were preconceived as worthier/holier and thence predestined, Arminius wins; if considered as sinners worthy of ruin and given faith by special mercy after election, we win
pass_a_gloss: Unto this returns the sum of this controversy: If in the everlasting decree of election and of reprobation certain persons were preconsidered by God as worthier than others, better and holier, and thence infallibly predestined unto life, and on the contrary certain others preconsidered as unto these unworthier, worse and more wicked, and thence excluded from predestination unto life, Arminius conquers, we fall from the cause: But if, on the contrary, as many as were predestined unto life before the foundations of the world were laid were considered by God as sinners worthy of everlasting destruction, by the special mercy of God, and a certain singular calling according to purpose, to be infallibly gifted with faith, repentance, perseverance, and salvation itself, yet not foreseen before their election as determining themselves before others by a right use of free choice from offered grace unto conceiving faith and persevering in the same.
pass_b_english: The sum of this controversy comes to this. If in the eternal decree of election and reprobation God preconceived certain persons as worthier, better, and holier than others, and thence infallibly predestined them to life — and preconceived others as unworthier, worse, and more wicked, and thence shut them out from predestination to life — Arminius wins, we lose the cause. But if, on the contrary side, all who were predestined to life before the world's foundations were laid were considered by God as sinners worthy of everlasting ruin, to be infallibly gifted — by God's special mercy and a singular calling according to purpose — with faith, repentance, perseverance, and salvation itself, and were not foreseen before their election as determining themselves ahead of others by a right use of free choice from offered grace to conceive faith and persevere in it.
source_text: Huc redit summa hujus controversiae: Si in aeterno decreto electionis et reprobationis personae quaedam fuerunt a Deo praeconsideratae tanquam aliis digniores, meliores et sanctiores, atque inde ad vitam infallibiliter praedestinatae, atque e contra aliae quaedam praeconsideratae ut hisce indigniores, nequiores et improbiores, atque inde a praedestinatione ad vitam exclusae, vincit Arminius, nos causa cadimus: Si autem, ex adverso, quotquot ad vitam fuerunt ante jacta mundi fundamenta praedestinati, fuerunt a Deo considerati ut peccatores aeterno exitio digni, per specialem misericordiam Dei, et singularem quandam et secundum propositum vocationem, fide, resipiscentia, perseverantia, ipsaque salute infallibiliter donandi, non autem praevisi ante electionem suam tanquam prae aliis recto liberi arbitrii usu ex oblata gratia ad concipiendam fidem in eaque perseverandum sese determinantes.
